title: Verifier Truth — the machinery that watches the machinery
prerequisite: M29 and M44 completion bars met, and the M53 lane integration accepted — re-audited by G1 on every run through the persisted closure records and the 40-gate lane ladder record
laneDiscipline: D-7: script/m61/* and validation/m61/* only (plus docs/m61/*); co-agent lanes (M14/M37/M59/M60) are read-only

issues.scope: the M61 ledger; seal verification of every trusted record (V1); lock discipline (V2); the bar re-audit that re-executes V1–V6 on every run; the chain wiring audit
acceptanceCriteria: gate exits 0 only on a fully verified ledger; a hollow closure, a removed issue, a mis-ordered group, a lane escape, a tampered record and an unwired gate each FAIL (proven by in-memory negatives)
this run's own ledger entry is written from measurements and validated whole, never asserted
the lane's own bars (M29/M44 closures, M53 integration + ladder) are re-audited here on every run
closureRequirements: G1 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
the bar re-audit reports V1–V6 green in the same run
verify-chain wiring present

evidence.blockedReason: Bar re-audit re-executes V1–V6 (the milestone's own gates). The LANE bar (m24→m44) is re-audited transitively through the persisted closures and the ladder record listed in the prerequisite block — re-running the 41-gate ladder here would cost ~40 minutes per governance run and is X1's job.

issues.scope: ONE evidence write/read path carrying a sha256 seal over the record content; migration for the legacy unsealed corpus; adoption across the IDE-lane gates
acceptanceCriteria: every evidence record is written through writeSealed and read through the trusted path; a tampered, half-written or hand-edited record is refused, never believed
the migration re-seals legacy records with field preservation; the transition window warns on legacy, fails on new
mutants prove tamper detection, wrong-payload hashing, seal-skipping writes and lossy migration
closureRequirements: V1 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
the lane's write/read adoption audited; the residue declared with reasons
mutants prove every seal law can fail

issues.scope: a declared lock per results dir: bounded wait, loud refusal, stale detection that never silently steals, reentrancy within a process
acceptanceCriteria: a second writer waits (bounded) and then REFUSES with a reason; it never silently steals a stale lock or clobbers a record
the lock is integrated at the one write path, so no gate can opt out
mutants prove release, stale detection, the refusal path and the concurrent-run serialization
closureRequirements: V2 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
a real-process refusal recorded, and 200 concurrent writes each landing exactly once
no lock file left behind by any lane results dir

issues.scope: an auditor that re-executes the recorded command of a DECLARED evidence sample inside an isolated worktree of HEAD and diffs the fresh record against the stored one field by field
acceptanceCriteria: the sample is declared, not chosen ad hoc; every member reproduces or is BLOCKED with its reason (a missing runtime is never recorded as non-reproducibility)
a timeout/signal kill is distinguished from a command failure — the m53 RC=124 lesson, made machinery
mutants prove a doctored record, a silent skip and an in-place clobber are all caught
closureRequirements: V3 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
the declared sample reproduced with the stored evidence byte-unchanged
the auditor wired into both chains

evidence.blockedReason: The sample is runtime-light by design (component-level gates): the audit proves the recorded commands reproduce, not that every heavy editor/giant-repo leg does. Heavy legs are re-run by their own milestone closures; extending the sample is a one-line change to the sample file.

issues.scope: the verifier lint: gate/record census, attribution, sealing, can-fail floor, execution-tier wiring, declared env vars, static import order, and record-must-agree-with-the-run
acceptanceCriteria: every lane script is a gate that owns a sealed record or a declared non-gate with a reason; every orphan record is a declared artifact
every gate carries the declared can-fail floor or a declared no-can-fail reason; every gate is in an execution tier or declared on-demand with one
mutants prove each rule can fail (canfail, seal, orphan, floor, env, tier, import order, record order)
closureRequirements: V4 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
the lint green over the real lane with a reported census
the lint wired into both chains

evidence.blockedReason: Gate membership is derived from the evidence (a record names its gate, or the gate's source names the record) — a gate that writes no record is invisible to the derivation and is caught by G1 instead.

issues.scope: every published number re-derived at gate-run time from the evidence it cites, with the audit set DECLARED over README + website + docs
acceptanceCriteria: a row-anchored template is rendered from the derived values and must appear verbatim in its doc; a mismatch is drift
the coverage set is declared: a doc publishing this lane's counts is pinned, and a doc declared out-of-scope that publishes one fails
mutants prove a prose edit, a blocked derivation, an unfilled template, a broken registry, a dead scan and both coverage defects
closureRequirements: V5 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
the coverage census reported (published vs pinned) with the residue visible
the pins wired into both chains

evidence.blockedReason: The tool pins the claims DECLARED in script/m61/claims.json, and coverage (#846's audit set: README + website + docs) is enforced by the scan — an out-of-scope doc that publishes a lane count fails. The residue on the pinned doc is reported as the `coverage` census rather than hidden: a count-claim line not covered by a pin is visible in the record and is the registry's next extension.

issues.scope: the bug-class extinction pack: every historical verifier-bug class carries a permanent mutant in the gate that owns it, traced to its incident, in an automated tier, recorded in that gate's sealed evidence
acceptanceCriteria: six declared classes (TDZ import, silent capability cap, self-staling byte-gated doc, concurrent clobber, unsealed evidence trust, on-demand gate rot) each proven extinct from live facts
every mutant carries a comment naming the incident it memorializes
mutants prove the pack fails on a missing mutant, an untraced mutant, an unwired mutant gate and a proof-less record
closureRequirements: V6 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
the six classes' owning gates carry their mutants with can-fail proofs in their records
the pack wired into both chains

evidence.blockedReason: Presence is a source fact: this gate proves the mutant exists, is traced, is wired, and that its owner's sealed record shows it ran. It does not re-execute every owner (two of them are heavy measurement gates) — re-execution is the lane ladder's and X1's job.

issues.scope: the program-closure audit: M61's ledger plus the IDE lane (m24/m29/m42/m44/m55 closures, and the 40-gate ladder record) re-audited at HEAD, with the spot-check pack the owner's verdict is made from
acceptanceCriteria: X1 green at the closing HEAD with the full-lane re-audit run sequentially (V2 discipline)
at least 5 mutants; the known-gaps inventory is generated from the records and byte-gated
the spot-check pack is present and names every issue; the verdict stays the owner's
closureRequirements: X1 evidence (verified, sealed) at the closing HEAD
all M61 issues closed with pinned evidence
the owner verdict per the IDE Honesty Contract §8 evidence rules (5) recorded, not inferred

evidence.blockedReason: X1 is the auditor, so its own ledger entry is written from THIS run's measurements (the projection rule) and then validated whole — a pre-existing pin would make a fresh HEAD unverifiable, and the m29 self-referential-trap rationale applies.
